- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile.  
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., > -0.50) — model tends to ignore bearish sentiment.  
- Forecast mean reversion too aggressively after sharp moves — model overcorrects early, then undercorrects later.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price by 5–10% relative to prior 18-day average.  
- Avoid over-optimistic 30-day forecasts when recent 18-day history shows strong downward momentum — sentiment and price divergence signal caution.  
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model often overshoots — cap forecast increase to 3–5% above prior 18-day mean.
